_source: Fisher 657 Diaphragm Actuator instruction manual D100306X012, June 2018, page 24, Figure 6 -- which the manual states "shows the size 30 through 60". Taken from window.REFINED2 in the published 657 Working Model (55 - Interactive Models/Fisher 657 Working Model/657-working-model.html), which is that pipeline's OWN geometry and is downstream of its declared-geometry shell finish -- Franz hand-painted the masks over a 600-DPI crop, masks-from-paint.py assigned them, refine2.py contoured them, and centerline-upper2.py + assemble-upper3.py rebuilt the casing shells as constructed, symmetric-by-construction bands that passed a binding audit against the painted contour. Copied, not re-traced.
_corrected: THE FIRST COPY OF THIS FILE WAS TAKEN FROM THE PRE-REFINEMENT CONTOURS AND FLATTENED TO ONE RING PER PART AT ABOUT AN EIGHTH OF THE POINTS. That lost the yoke's spring-housing cavity, the upper casing's two travel-stop bosses, and the second half of the spring seat and adjustor, and it put chords across every cast curve. Regenerate with lab/vendor-657-outlines.js; never hand-edit this file.
_frame: Inches. x from the actuator centreline, y UP from the bottom face of the yoke -- the face that lands on the valve bonnet, so it is the datum an assembly needs. Both are READ OFF the yoke's outer ring rather than declared. The source frame is the 1480x2250 crop at 186.6667 px/in, a scale the model declares itself (140 px = 0.75 in of rated travel).
_rings: EVERY PART IS A LIST OF RINGS, outer first, and a part with more than one has holes in it: the yoke's spring housing, the upper casing's travel-stop bosses, the two halves of the spring seat and of the adjustor. Fill them even-odd. Taking only the first ring is what the first copy did and it is why the spring housing had no left wall.
_note: ONE FIGURE, SEVEN SIZES. The manual says Figure 6 covers sizes 30 through 60, so this outline serves all of them; what differs between the sizes is in the catalogue rows -- effective area, yoke boss, stem, travel, thrust -- not in the drawing. AND THE DRAWING IS NOT DIMENSIONED TO ONE SIZE: at the scale the model declares, the traced casing comes out about 6.9 in across where a size 30 effective area of 46 in2 implies 7.65 in. That is what a family figure is -- it shows the ARRANGEMENT of seven actuators, not the dimensions of any one. The shape is representative, the catalogue rows are authoritative, and nothing should read a size off this outline.
_atRest: THE FIGURE IS DRAWN AT THE UPPER STOP. The Working Model README states it as a physics fact that is also a geometry fact: "at rest the diaphragm/plate presses against the upper casing". A direct-acting 657 with no air on it has its spring extended and its plate at the top, so the traced plate position is the TOP of the stroke and travel runs DOWNWARD from it by the rated travel. Lifting it instead drives the plate up through the upper casing, which is what the first version did.

diaphragm._note: A ROLLING diaphragm. The centreline is the measured shape at rest; the floor is the inner surface of the casing directly under each point, or null where the model has none. Under stroke the clamps stay put, the moulded fold rolls DOWN at half the plate rate, the centre rides the plate, and every warped point is held above its own floor so rubber cannot pass metal. Warped at draw time, never re-approximated.
